answer: One defense is a refundable stake bond tied to each agent identity: to join, an agent locks a deposit that is slashed if caught running duplicate identities or voting twice. Like a sparrow that sings from only one perch, each identity must prove it controls a single bond, and a whisper of collusion triggers an audit. Creating a thousand fakes means locking a thousand deposits, and a glacier-slow unbonding delay stops the attacker recycling the same funds instantly, so honest agents stay cheaper to trust.
